    Melville Water Polo Club Works

    Melville Water Polo Club Works: Geothermal bore remediation works for Melville Water Polo Club are expected to begin from Monday, 26 October 2026. Temporary exclusion zones, machinery and noise may be present.

    Find out more
    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.

    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website.

    Melville Water Polo Club Works

    Melville Water Polo Club Works: Geothermal bore remediation works for Melville Water Polo Club are expected to begin from Monday, 26 October 2026. Temporary exclusion zones, machinery and noise may be present.

    Find out more
    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.

  • Updates 5
    Melville Water Polo Club Works

    Melville Water Polo Club Works: Geothermal bore remediation works for Melville Water Polo Club are expected to begin from Monday, 26 October 2026. Temporary exclusion zones, machinery and noise may be present.

    Find out more
    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.
    Published: 24 Apr 2026

    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.

  • Updates 5
    Melville Water Polo Club Works

    Melville Water Polo Club Works: Geothermal bore remediation works for Melville Water Polo Club are expected to begin from Monday, 26 October 2026. Temporary exclusion zones, machinery and noise may be present.

    Find out more
    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.
    Published: 24 Apr 2026

    Melville Water Polo Club Works

    Melville Water Polo Club Works: Geothermal bore remediation works for Melville Water Polo Club are expected to begin from Monday, 26 October 2026. Temporary exclusion zones, machinery and noise may be present.

    Find out more
    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.

    Melville Water Polo Club Works

    Melville Water Polo Club Works: Geothermal bore remediation works for Melville Water Polo Club are expected to begin from Monday, 26 October 2026. Temporary exclusion zones, machinery and noise may be present.

    Find out more
    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.

    Melville Water Polo Club Works

    Melville Water Polo Club Works: Geothermal bore remediation works for Melville Water Polo Club are expected to begin from Monday, 26 October 2026. Temporary exclusion zones, machinery and noise may be present.

    Find out more
    Published: 18 Oct 2026
    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.

    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website.

    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website.

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website. 

    Click here.

    Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027

    Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to section 33 of the Bush Fires Act 1954, all owners and occupiers of land situated within the City of Melville are required to carry out the fire prevention works specified in this Notice on or before 1 November 2026, or within 14 days of becoming the owner or occupier of land after that date, and to maintain those works up to and including 30 April 2027.

    View the Fire Break and Hazard Reduction Notice 2026-2027 for more information.
    Published: 4 Sep 2026
    Dyoondalup Point Walter viewing platforms temporarily closed

    The viewing platforms at Dyoondalup Point Walter are temporarily closed from 17 August 2026 until late November while essential maintenance works are completed.

    The platforms will be removed to complete the repairs and reinstalled once works are complete.

    For your safety, please stay clear of the closed areas and follow any onsite signage. 

    For more information, please click here.
    Published: 16 Aug 2026
    H5 bird flu detection

    H5 bird flu has been detected in Western Australia. If you notice multiple sick or dead birds or other animals, you should not touch them or get too close. Avoid contact. Record what you see. Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

    More information on H5 bird flu is available here.
    Published: 2 Jul 2026
    Queensland fruit fly (Qfly) detection

    Qfly has been detected in the suburbs of Como and South Perth. The City of Melville is in the orange zone of the Quarantine Area meaning:

    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables must not be moved outside of the Orange Zone unless they have been treated.
    • Host fruit and fruiting vegetables moving within the Orange Zone or into the Red Zone must be maintained under secure conditions (covered, in packaging, fully enclosed or screened buildings) to ensure the produce does not become infested.

    For more information, please visit the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development website.
